text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria expects to receive $80 million World Bank loan to support the country's pension payments and to stimulate private business initiatives of people to be laid off due to the structural reform, Labour and Social policy minister Ivan Neikov said.

-- Bulgaria hopes that the European Union member countries will waive visa requirements for its citizens after the country introduces new legal amendments in line with the EU requirements, Justice minister Vassil Gotsev said.
Bulgaria is on the EU's Schengen list of countries with restrictive access to the EU member states.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had sold 68 percent of vegetable oil producer Kambana to the Rotterdam-based Helian Commodities BV for $5.5 million.

-- Bulgaria will secure a minimum farm gate price of $130 per tonne of wheat from this year's harvest for local producers in a bid to limit wheat exports and avert a possible grain shortage, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.
-- Bulgaria's Transport minister Wilhelm Kraus said funding has been found for selecting a consultant for the sale of the country's state carrier Balkan Airlines.
-- Bulgaria's new government may fail to implement its four-year stabilisation programme if it does not solve current problems in its relations with Russia, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said. @
Kostov formally invited Russia's Prime minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to visit Sofia by the end of this year.

-- Bulgaria's parliament passed on first, preliminary reading the Banking Bill which sets stricter licensing rules and empowers the central bank to cancel licences of insolvent banks without right of appeal.
The parliament is expected to debate and pass the Banking Bill and amend the Bulgarian National Bank law on second and final reading next week.

-- Bulgaria's international cargo and passenger road transport companies will have to pay one million levs for three-year licences under a Transport ministry draft bill which is expected to be submitted for consideration to the government in the next couple of months.
-- Bulgaria has received bids for its military plants from investors which will introduce NATO production standards, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to raise excise fees on gambling to 13 million levs from nine million levs annually per a roulette table in local casinos, parliamentary budget commission chairman Yordan Tsonev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
